details: Current policy analysis covers return/status/public writes, but a theorem needs to show every admitted non-confidential entrypoint has gas/storage/boundary/object-schedule/opcode behavior determined only by public data. TB-01 suggests this theorem is currently false.

gap: End-to-end admitted-artifact noninterference theorem should be stated as the main theorem
details: The main theorem should quantify over two executions of the same admitted package with equal public inputs and equal declassification functions, and conclude equality/indistinguishability of the complete normalized hostile-host observer. Current routes package many interfaces and pair boundaries, but the human-facing theorem should expose this relation directly.

gap: Adaptive history theorem is only conditional
details: HistorySemantics.lean proves projections equal if HistoryStepsPublicEq is already assumed. It does not appear to derive stepwise equality from single-call UO plus a public adaptive strategy.
The final-public-state surface should prove the same commit/rollback behavior in IR, runtime, and public trace. See TB-04.

gap: Relational declassification theorem is too weak/coarse
details: Labels such as return/success/public_state object should be turned into explicit release functions. The theorem should prove noninterference modulo only those functions, and the checker should reject extraneous labels if least-release is intended.
Exact-field checks prove the current view is well-shaped, not that the view contains every runtime field that can influence observer behavior. A generated coverage theorem would reduce this trust.

The docs explicitly use modulo uint256 arithmetic and div/mod-by-zero = 0, diverging from Solidity 0.8. A theorem should either call the source language a Solidity-like DSL or prove a translation relation from a selected Solidity semantics/pragma subset.

gap: Checker/admission theorem should include full V and deployment binding
details: The claim says admitted package (P,M,V); theorem framing should require exact compiler/proof/runtime model and deployment-attestation hashes, or explicitly separate theorem admission from deployment.

gap: ORAM cap/resource predicate not fully mirrored in Lean imported shape
details: If capacity <= 128 is part of the proof-grade theorem route, it should be in the Lean admission predicate; if not, it should be documented as implementation practicality only.
